small_guidance:
- The K-loop reloads the same x tile for every oc_start iteration; swap the loop order so OC is the inner accumulator: keep `acc[BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N]` blocks per oc tile, but iterate K in the outer loop and load `x_vals[BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N]` once, reusing it across all OC tiles via a register-resident array — or simpler, fuse all of OC into BLOCK_M (OC=128 fits in one tile of BLOCK_M=128) so the K-loop runs only once per program.
- With OC=128, set BLOCK_M=128 fixed (single oc tile, no outer oc_start loop) and autotune only BLOCK_N ∈ {64,128,256} and BLOCK_K ∈ {32,64} at num_warps=8, num_stages=2-3 — verify `(128·BK + BK·BN)·4·stages ≤ 132KB`.
- Add a `(64,128,32,nw=4,ns=3)` and `(128,64,64,nw=4,ns=2)` config; the current best is likely BLOCK_N=128 but stages=3 will improve K-loop overlap given the redundant x-reloads.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as a single-pass im2col GEMM where each program owns one (N, output-spatial tile) and accumulates the **full** OC×BLOCK_N tile in registers (OC=128 fits one BLOCK_M=128 tile). This eliminates the outer `for oc_start` loop and the redundant x_vals reloads — the dominant inefficiency right now is that each x element is read OC/BLOCK_M times.
- Fuse the channel-min reduction online: after computing the full OC column for each spatial element, reduce across OC inside registers (tl.min over axis=0) and store only the min, never materializing the OC×OUT_HW conv output to global memory. Current kernel already does this conceptually but pays for it by re-running the GEMM per oc tile.
- Use channels-last (NHWC) input layout so the GEMM-K axis (IC·KH·KW) is contiguous and x loads coalesce across BLOCK_K; reorder weight to (OC, KH, KW, IC) at init. Keep KH=KW=3 unrolled as a constexpr loop over 9 positions, with a BLOCK_K that walks IC contiguously — this turns the gather into a near-pure stride-1 load.
